Event.description:
A generic timed observation.

The vocabulary is open: ``type`` is a namespaced string rather than an enum,
so a new kind of observation is a new namespace and not a schema change.
Anything specific to a kind lives in ``payload`` under that same namespace.

confidence.description: Producer's confidence, where the producer reports one. Absence of an event is never evidence of absence in the audio; see docs/architecture.md.
confidence.title: Confidence

payload.description: Type-specific data, keyed within the event type's own namespace.
payload.title: Payload

start_s.description: Start time in the timeline's time unit.
start_s.title: Start S

Event.title: Event

Evidence.description:
What an event is grounded in.

The event's own ``start_s``/``end_s`` are the source interval; this names the
artifact that interval belongs to and the stage that read it. An event with
no traceable evidence is an assertion, and this contract has no room for one.

artifact.description: Artifact this observation came from, e.g. 'source' or 'stems/bass.wav'.
artifact.title: Artifact

stage.description: Name of the producing stage in this timeline's provenance.
stage.title: Stage

Evidence.title: Evidence

Provenance.description:
One producing stage, recorded so its output can be attributed and recomputed.

A stage entry answers: which inputs, which tool at which exact revision, with
which parameters, on which runtime, for how long, emitting which artifacts,
and at which truth layer. Together with the input hashes it is also the
cache key: an entry whose key cannot be recomputed is garbage, not a cache.

input_hashes.description: Role name to content hash for every input this stage consumed.
input_hashes.title: Input Hashes

output_hashes.description: Role name to content hash for every artifact this stage emitted.
output_hashes.title: Output Hashes

parameters.description: Parameters that affected the result, and therefore the cache key.
parameters.title: Parameters

runtime.description: Runtime and backend actually used, e.g. 'cpython3.11 macos-arm64 mps'.
runtime.title: Runtime

stage.description: Stage name, unique within a timeline, e.g. 'separation' or 'onsets.bass'.
stage.title: Stage

tool_revision.description: Exact revision of that tool: a version plus commit, never a branch.
tool_revision.title: Tool Revision

Provenance.title: Provenance

SourceAudio.description: The evidence-bearing artifact this timeline is about.

hash.description: Hash of the exact audio bytes the stages consumed.
hash.title: Hash

SourceAudio.title: SourceAudio

Track.description: A logical stream of observations, usually but not necessarily one stem.

role.description: Free-text role, e.g. 'bass'. A label for humans, not a taxonomy.
role.title: Role

source.description: Artifact these observations came from, e.g. 'mix' or 'stems/drums.wav'.
source.title: Source

Track.title: Track

TruthLayer.description:
Where a value came from. These never collapse into one another.

``requested``
    Authored before the audio existed. A prompt, a seed, a target BPM.
``observed``
    Measurable from the artifact by anyone holding it. A duration, a hash.
``inferred``
    A named model's opinion at an exact revision, with a confidence.
``corrected``
    A human override, recorded as its own stage rather than as an edit that
    erases the inference it replaced.
TruthLayer.title: TruthLayer

description: The compiler boundary artifact: what was observed or inferred about one recording.

provenance.description: Every stage that contributed to this document, in production order.
provenance.title: Provenance

time_unit.description: Explicit, because a timeline read years later must not have to guess.
time_unit.title: Time Unit
